evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and silhouette read clearly as a round-headed archway in a wall section; top view is a plain rectangle, as expected for a 2-stud-deep modular wall piece.
evidence.V2: Some hierarchy (wall slab, stacked jamb blocks, voussoir ring, small gold keystone) but the upper half is a large blank slab with only a thin coping, so medium/small detail is concentrated in a narrow band.
evidence.V3: Symmetric and correct (A15 X 0.0, T1 tiling pass) but the forms are stiff: a flat rectangular slab with a narrow, tall opening and evenly stacked box jambs; little exaggeration beyond the keystone.
evidence.V4: Consistent chamfers on coping, jamb blocks, voussoirs and keystone catch the light in the keystone, springing and end-section close-ups.
evidence.V5: Clean smooth shading; no pinches, seams or z-fighting in keystone, springing or end-section close-ups.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: stone hue in three values (light springer blocks, mid wall, dark plinth course) plus a single gold keystone.
evidence.V7: 660 tris vs module target 800: at target.
evidence.V8: One LF_VertexColor material, stone main hue with gold keystone, kit-sized chamfers, 2-stud grid footprint (T1 pass); matches kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Anchored, Default collision to keep the opening walkable, CanTouch off, grid-corner pivot, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic; all gates pass.

top_fixes: Break up the blank upper wall: add a few coursed blocks or a string course above the arch, or raise the arch so the spandrel is smaller
Widen the opening and/or make the keystone and voussoirs larger and more exaggerated for a confident stylised read
Let the jamb blocks vary slightly in height or offset for a less mechanical stack
